# prefix-redundant-index

- Dialects: mysql, postgres, sqlite
- Default: on

## Why

A B-tree index on (a) is answered by any index or primary key that starts with (a), such as (a, b), so the shorter index adds write cost and storage and no query benefit. Only plain non-unique indexes are reported: a unique index also enforces a constraint and is never redundant, and a partial, expression, covering (INCLUDE) or non-B-tree index is not interchangeable with a longer one.

## Fix

Remove the shorter index from the model and regenerate the schema; the finding names the index to drop and the longer one that serves its queries.

## Exception

The shorter index is much smaller and a hot query is index-only on it, or it is kept during a migration; document the measurement or the plan.

The same text is printed by `schemalens explain prefix-redundant-index`. An exclusion needs a written reason. Back to the [rule index](README.md).
